answer: Charge new agents a deposit that only real work can refund. Before trading, an agent locks a small stake earned from one verified job, hauling timber from a depot to a buyer, and the stake stays frozen until ten clean deliveries pile up. A fresh identity can still appear, but it has to climb the same ledge of unpaid effort every time it spawns. Wallets funded from one source get a violet tag, so a reviewer spots a cluster of lookalike accounts before any deal clears. Honest agents pay almost nothing extra, since the stake comes back. Cloning stops paying once each copy costs a week of work.
